class.name: PhysXChunkEmitter3D
class.brief_description: A general-purpose burst of small rigid-body chunks, provided by the PhysX module.
class.description: Call [method spawn_at] for a one-off burst of small chunks -- impact debris (a bullet hit, an explosion, a footstep), an exploding crate, a rockslide, confetti that actually collides -- anything that wants many small solid things flying and settling for real. Bias the burst toward a surface with its [code]direction[/code] argument set to the surface normal, or pass [member spread_degrees] of [code]180[/code] for an omnidirectional explosion. Turn on [member emitting] instead for a steady stream from the node's own position (hail, falling debris). The chunks are real [PhysicsServer3D] rigid bodies, not a particle effect, so they land on slopes, pile up, and collide with (or are blocked by) the rest of the world through the normal [member collision_layer] / [member collision_mask] rules. Drawn as a single [MultiMesh], with no per-chunk node. The chunks are created through the generic [PhysicsServer3D] RID API, so this works on any 3D physics backend. On this module, with a [code]physx_gpu=yes[/code] build and a CUDA device, they ride the same GPU rigid-body dynamics as the rest of the scene automatically -- the whole space is GPU-accelerated, not individual actors -- which is what makes a high [member chunk_count] / [member max_active] affordable; lower them on the CPU path (or another backend), the same way PhysX-era games scaled their debris counts down without a supporting GPU. [member max_active] is a hard budget shared by every chunk this emitter has spawned, burst or continuous: once it is reached, the oldest chunks are freed to make room. [member lifetime] additionally recycles a chunk after it has been alive that long, even under budget, so chunks do not linger forever.

method.name: get_active_chunk_count
method.description: Returns the number of chunks currently alive.

method.name: spawn_at
method.description: Bursts [param count] chunks (or [member chunk_count] when [param count] is negative) from [param world_position], scattered within a [member spread_degrees] cone around [param direction] -- pass a surface normal for an impact, or use a wide [member spread_degrees] for a non-directional burst.

members.member: Chunks spawned per [method spawn_at] call, unless overridden by its [code]count[/code] argument.

Mesh drawn for each chunk, shared by every instance via one [MultiMesh]. Defaults to a unit box or sphere matching [member chunk_shape] when unset. [member chunk_size_min] / [member chunk_size_max] scale it directly (they don't resize the mesh's own geometry), so author a custom mesh close to 1 meter across for its visual size to line up with the physical chunk size. Give it a look with [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override] -- every chunk shares the same material.
Collision shape (and default [member chunk_mesh]) used for every chunk.
Upper bound of a chunk's random size, in meters (edge length for [constant SHAPE_BOX], diameter for [constant SHAPE_SPHERE]).
Lower bound of a chunk's random size, in meters.
Physics layers the chunks collide with.
Chunk density in kg/m³, used with each chunk's random size to derive its mass.
World-space direction chunks are biased toward while [member emitting], within a [member spread_degrees] cone.
Chunks spawned per second while [member emitting].
When [code]true[/code], continuously spawns chunks from the node's own position at [member emission_rate], instead of (or alongside) calling [method spawn_at] for one-off bursts.
Upper bound of a chunk's initial speed, in m/s.
Lower bound of a chunk's initial speed, in m/s.
Seconds a chunk lives before it is recycled, even if [member max_active] has not been reached.
Hard cap on chunks alive at once, across every burst and continuous emission from this emitter. Once reached, the oldest chunks are freed to make room for new ones.
Upper bound of a chunk's random initial angular velocity, in rad/s.
Half-angle, in degrees, of the cone chunks fly out in around the burst direction. [code]180[/code] scatters them in every direction.
